newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HIDEKI IRABU IMPRESSIVE IN FIRST MINOR-LEAGUE START.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HIDEKI IRABU IMPRESSIVE IN FIRST MINOR-LEAGUE START.

text.p: Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu, who signed a four-year, $12.8 million contract with the New York Yankees last month, was impressive in his eagerly-anticipated minor-league debut for Class-A Tampa in a Florida State League game on Tuesday.
Irabu pitched four scoreless innings against the Port St. Lucie Mets at Legends Field in Tampa. He allowed just one hit with no walks and six strikeouts.
Irabu, touted as the Japanese Nolan Ryan for his strikeout prowess, threw 42 pitches and was clocked consistently near 100 miles-per-hour (161 kph).
The hard-throwing right-hander is expected to make two or three starts for Tampa and a few more with Triple-A Columbus before joining the Yankees sometime around the July All-Star Game break.
The San Diego Padres owned the rights to the 28-year-old Irabu as a result of their working agreement with the pitcher's Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines.
But Irabu was steadfast in his desire to pitch only for the Yankees and was prepared to sit out the entire season if he was not traded to the World Series champions.
Months of negotiations between the Yankees and Padres and weeks more between the Yanks and Irabu's agent finally landed the Japanese star in pinstripes late last month.
He was 12-6 and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season.

Irabu will become the fourth Japanese player in the major leagues, joining three other pitchers -- Hideo Nomo of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shigetoshi Hasegawa of the Anaheim Angels and Takashi Kashiwada of the New York Mets.
